experiment: Cycle 1 compares canonical, a 25-percent phase-diverse homogeneous replacement, and a 25-percent target-invariant mixed-prefix replacement under ordinary learned Attention for L19 seeds 1/2/4 and L18 seed 2.
reason: The matched pair changes only whether the four special batches in each deterministic block mix token families. It keeps 320 steps, eight supervised rows per step, aggregate token and target histograms, family exposure, optimizer, seed, and intervention cadence fixed.
negative_controls: canonical bitwise reproduction; matched phase-diverse homogeneous schedule; deterministic duplicate; L18 seed 2 scope control; ordinary-Attention activity guard

experiment: Reorder the exact cycle-1 mixed-invariance multiset into MIXED_FIRST and MIXED_LAST curricula. Each run contains the same 80 mixed batches and 240 canonical homogeneous batches as the interleaved arm, with identical per-row inputs and targets; only order changes.
reason: Cycle 1 nearly stabilizes seed 2 but misses the preregistered token threshold by four. Same-multiset ordering has higher discrimination than changing dose or optimizer and directly tests early shaping versus late forgetting.
negative_controls: cycle-1 matched homogeneous; exact same-multiset histogram; cycle-1 interleaved mixed; L18 seed 2; ordinary-Attention activity guard

experiment: Use the successful mixed-last curriculum at exactly two smaller fixed doses: 12.5 percent (40 mixed batches) and 6.25 percent (20 mixed batches), each with the remaining batches canonical homogeneous, across L19 seeds 1/2/4 and L18 seed 2.
reason: Both 25-percent orders pass, so order is not necessary at that dose. The remaining question is the smallest tested amount; two smaller powers-of-two exhaust the preregistered three-dose limit without hyperparameter search.
negative_controls: cycle-1 matched homogeneous; cycle-1 canonical; 25-percent interleaved/first/last results; L18 seed 2; ordinary-Attention activity guard
